Every command runs as `gitso <command>` (or `python gitso.py <command>`), and by its own
path. `gitso docs <command>` prints the same text in a terminal.

## Basic: one Git or host operation

### discover

`gitso discover`, or `Basic/discover.py`.

```text
Find Git repositories under a root. Read-only: a filesystem walk, no git, no network.

Why:          every larger operation starts by knowing which repositories exist.
Reads:        the folders under the root (no Git, no network).
May change:   nothing.
Results:      a list, or --json.
Layer:        Basic: one Git or host operation.
Status:       working

    python Basic/discover.py <root> [--json] [--max-depth N] [--hidden]
        [--cross-filesystems] [--no-skip]
```

### status

`gitso status`, or `Basic/status.py`.

```text
Report one repository's facts as JSON. Read-only.

Why:          every judgment above starts from one repository's plain facts.
Reads:        one repository.
May change:   nothing.
Results:      JSON on stdout.
Layer:        Basic: one Git or host operation.
Status:       working

    python Basic/status.py <repo-path>
```

### fetch

`gitso fetch`, or `Basic/fetch.py`.

```text
Fetch a repository's remote. Moves remote-tracking refs only.

Why:          "behind" must mean behind the remote now, not at the last fetch.
Reads:        the remote.
May change:   remote-tracking refs only; never a branch or a file.
Results:      a JSON result on stdout.
Layer:        Basic: one Git or host operation.
Status:       working

    python Basic/fetch.py <repo> [--remote origin] [--dry-run]

With no refspec, `git fetch` updates `refs/remotes/*` and never a local branch or the working
tree -- nothing the user would have to undo. That is why observation may fetch at all.
```

### pull

`gitso pull`, or `Basic/pull.py`.

```text
Fast-forward one repository to its upstream. Never merges, never rebases.

Why:          a fast-forward cannot lose work, so it is the one pull that needs no decision.
Reads:        the repository and its upstream.
May change:   the checked-out branch and its files, by fast-forward only.
Results:      a JSON result on stdout.
Layer:        Basic: one Git or host operation.
Status:       working

    python Basic/pull.py <repo>

`--ff-only` is the whole safety argument: a fast-forward cannot destroy data and never asks
for a choice, so when git cannot fast-forward it refuses, and the refusal is reported as a
failure for a human -- never resolved here. There is no option to do anything else.
Callers decide *whether* a repository qualifies (clean, behind-only); this only performs it.
```

### clone

`gitso clone`, or `Basic/clone.py`.

```text
Clone one repository into a destination that does not exist yet.

Why:          a clone may only ever add a folder.
Reads:        the remote URL; the user's own Git credentials.
May change:   creates the destination folder; refuses one that exists.
Results:      a JSON result on stdout.
Layer:        Basic: one Git or host operation.
Status:       working

    python Basic/clone.py <url> <destination> [--mirror] [--no-local]

Never clones over anything: an existing destination is refused before git runs, so a clone can
only ever add a folder. Credentials are the user's own (`gh auth setup-git`, an SSH agent);
with prompts disabled, a missing one fails fast instead of waiting on an invisible question.
```

### reset-keep

`gitso reset-keep`, or `Basic/reset_keep.py`.

```text
Move one repository's checked-out branch to another commit, keeping uncommitted edits.

Why:          following a rewritten history needs a branch move that never overwrites an edit.
Reads:        the repository and the target commit.
May change:   the checked-out branch and the files that differ; refuses over any uncommitted edit.
Results:      a JSON result on stdout.
Layer:        Basic: one Git or host operation.
Status:       working

    python Basic/reset_keep.py <repo> <target>

`git reset --keep` moves the branch and updates the files that differ between the two commits,
and refuses outright if any of those files has an uncommitted change -- so an edit is never
overwritten. There is no option for `--hard`, `--mixed` or `--soft`, and there must never be one:
the mirror of `pull --ff-only` and of a push that cannot force.

What it does **not** protect is commits. A commit on the branch that `target` does not contain is
left on no branch (still in the reflog, until git expires it). Deciding whether that is
acceptable -- proving nothing unpushed would be hidden, then asking the person -- belongs to the
caller. This only performs the move.
```

### commit

`gitso commit`, or `Basic/commit.py`.

```text
Commit the named files of one repository, and nothing else.

Why:          commits must contain exactly what was chosen, never everything that happens to be staged.
Reads:        the named paths in the working tree.
May change:   one new commit of exactly those paths; other staged work stays staged.
Results:      a JSON result on stdout.
Layer:        Basic: one Git or host operation.
Status:       working

    python Basic/commit.py <repo> -m MESSAGE PATH [PATH ...]

Only the paths given are committed -- added, changed or deleted -- even when other changes are
staged; those stay staged, untouched. There is no option for "everything" (`-a`), for rewriting
the last commit (`--amend`), for an empty commit, or for skipping the repository's hooks, and
there must never be one. A detached HEAD is refused: the commit would belong to no branch.

Each named path is committed as it is in the working tree (a partly staged file is committed
whole). If git refuses the commit -- a hook, a missing identity -- the named paths are left
staged and the failure is reported; nothing else in the index changes.

The identity on the commit is whatever git would use here (see `_facts.next_commit_identity`);
deciding whether that identity is the right one belongs to the caller, as does deciding *what*
to commit. This only performs it.
```

### push

`gitso push`, or `Basic/push.py`.

```text
Push one repository's current branch to its upstream. Never forced.

Why:          publishing must never overwrite what is on the remote.
Reads:        the current branch and its upstream.
May change:   the remote branch, by fast-forward only; never forced.
Results:      a JSON result on stdout.
Layer:        Basic: one Git or host operation.
Status:       working

    python Basic/push.py <repo>

A push without `--force` is refused by git itself unless it is a fast-forward of the remote:
the mirror image of `pull --ff-only`. There is no parameter here that could add `--force`,
`--force-with-lease`, a `+refspec`, or `--mirror`, and there must never be one. Deciding
*whether* to push (ahead-only, clean, freshly re-checked) belongs to the caller.
```

## Special: this machine, once

### enroll-machine

`gitso enroll-machine`, or `Special/enroll_machine.py`.

```text
Enroll this machine with the app: which library folders it holds, and how the app shows itself.

Why:          the tray and every local command work on this machine's libraries; nothing is
              inventoried until you name them, and a machine may hold several.
Reads:        the settings profile; `find` reads folder names where you tell it to look
              (a folder, or --whole-machine), only after you type LOOK.
May change:   the profile's machine identity, libraries and presentation choices (what the
              tray opens; the web view off, on this machine, or on your tailnet). Never a
              repository, and never a fleet: joining one is Elaborate/setup_fleet.py.
Results:      text on stdout.
Layer:        Special: this machine, once.
Status:       working

    python Special/enroll_machine.py                       # show
    python Special/enroll_machine.py find T:/ | --whole-machine
    python Special/enroll_machine.py add T:/Github [D:/More]   (asks you to type SCAN)
    python Special/enroll_machine.py remove D:/More
    python Special/enroll_machine.py presentation --face web --web loopback
```

### update-archive

`gitso update-archive`, or `Special/update_archive.py`.

```text
Fast-forward eligible existing repositories in one or more local archives.

Why:          reference collections fall behind; only safe fast-forwards should catch them up.
Reads:        the archive's checkouts.
May change:   without --scan-only: fast-forward of clean, eligible checkouts.
Results:      a result on stdout, or --json; reports and logs as settings choose.
Layer:        Special: this machine, once.
Status:       working

    python Special/update_archive.py --help
    python Special/update_archive.py --root /path/to/archive --scan-only

Without --scan-only this updates clean eligible checkouts. It does not clone missing repos.
Saved roots/output/logging preferences are optional. --json gives a machine-readable result;
--no-report forces stdout only and --no-log disables operational logging. Reports are off by
default; local counts-only logs default on. Importing performs no operation.
```

### archive-manager

`gitso archive-manager`, or `Special/archive_manager.py`.

```text
Register local archive folders and refresh them using their saved update or sync mode.

Why:          archives you keep should refresh the way you chose for each, with one command.
Reads:        registered archives and their saved update or sync mode.
May change:   registrations; launchers when asked; the checkouts a refresh updates or clones.
Results:      a masked result on stdout, or JSON; reports and logs as settings choose.
Layer:        Special: this machine, once.
Status:       working

    python Special/archive_manager.py --help
    python Special/archive_manager.py --install /path/to/archive --mode update
    python Special/archive_manager.py --list
    python Special/archive_manager.py --refresh-all --scan-only --json --no-report --no-log
    python Special/archive_manager.py --refresh /path/to/archive --settings-home /path/to/profile

--install creates a launcher that resolves saved choices at run time. --forget removes the
registration only; common-profile receipts and launchers remain for ownership review. Existing
common settings own choices; legacy-only profiles retain their registry without migration.
Use Elaborate/schedule_archives.py for scheduling. Importing performs no operation.

Refresh calls run_refresh headlessly: saved update/sync mode per archive, one masked result,
optional aggregate report, shared counts-only logging. --output-mode/--output-dir/--json and
--log/--no-log/--log-dir override manager preferences. Reports default off; selected invalid
sinks fail without fallback. --scan-only leaves receipts unchanged. Action receipts contain
run status, not a guessed last report; actual report/log destinations are result artifacts.
Import run_refresh for programmatic use; it prints nothing and replaces no process streams.
```

### sync-archive

`gitso sync-archive`, or `Special/sync_archive.py`.

```text
Plan archives or explicitly update, sync, repair or publish them.

Why:          an archive should match what its host says should be there.
Reads:        the archive's checkouts and the host's repository list (through gh).
May change:   with the chosen action: clones, fast-forwards, origin repairs; with --publish, checked non-forced pushes.
Results:      a plan or result on stdout, or JSON; reports and logs as settings choose.
Layer:        Special: this machine, once.
Status:       working

    python Special/sync_archive.py --help
    python Special/sync_archive.py --root /path/to/archive --json --no-log
    python Special/sync_archive.py --root /path/to/archive --sync --yes

Default use plans to stdout; saved output/log preferences and explicit flags select channels.
Publication is a separate action: exact planned tips/targets pass outgoing-history security
checks before any non-force push. Masked findings are included in the shared result.
--dry-run never approves security. No registration, enrollment or setup is implied.
Import run_archives for headless use with explicit settings, requests and approval callback.
```

### export-inventory

`gitso export-inventory`, or `Special/export_inventory.py`.

```text
Record where every repository came from, so another machine can clone them.

Why:          another machine can only rebuild a library it has a record of.
Reads:        the repositories under the given roots and their remotes.
May change:   nothing.
Results:      one JSON inventory on stdout or --out; progress on stderr.
Layer:        Special: this machine, once.
Status:       working

    python Special/export_inventory.py [--root [LABEL=]PATH ...] [--repo PATH ...] [--out FILE]
        [--max-depth N] [--hidden] [--no-prompt] [--answers FILE]

Where the repositories are:
  --root   a folder that contains repositories (repeat for several, on any drives). A bare path
           is labelled by its own folder name; `label=path` names it yourself.
  --repo   one repository that lives somewhere on its own (repeat as needed). These are kept
           together under the reserved label `loose`, each remembering where it was.
  Neither given, at a terminal: a folder dialog asks, and keeps asking "add another?" until done.

Where the record goes: stdout, as one JSON document, with progress and the summary on stderr, so
`inventory_export.py --root X > inventory.json` is a complete inventory. `--out FILE` writes it
there instead. A run with no folders named, at a terminal, is the guided path: it also asks where
to save. The record names every repository, private ones included, so it must never be committed:
`--out` is checked before scanning and refuses an existing file, a link, and a tracked or
unignored path inside a Git work tree. Nothing is written beside this source checkout by default.

Paths inside the record are relative to their label, never a drive letter, so each label can land
anywhere on restore. Per repository: every remote URL (credentials stripped), host/owner/name,
branch, head, last commit, flags for what a clone cannot bring back, and whatever the repository
says about itself (readme, project files, `.git/description`, URLs found in them) -- including
repositories with no remote. Observation only: git reads, no network, at most the one chosen file.
```

### restore-inventory

`gitso restore-inventory`, or `Special/restore_inventory.py`.

```text
Clone the repositories in an inventory file onto this machine. Clone-only; never over anything.

Why:          rebuilding a library from an inventory should never clone over anything.
Reads:        an inventory file.
May change:   with --apply: new clones only, into the chosen folders.
Results:      the plan, then the results, on stdout.
Layer:        Special: this machine, once.
Status:       working

    python Special/restore_inventory.py [INVENTORY] [--map LABEL=DEST ...] [--dest DIR]
        [--layout preserve|canonical] [--only LABEL ...] [--use-candidates]
        [--apply] [--yes] [--no-prompt] [--answers FILE]

The inventory: the path given, else a file dialog (or terminal prompt) asks for it.

Where things go. Each label in the file (a root, or `loose` for repositories that lived on their
own) needs a destination on THIS machine, any drive, any folder; it is created on apply:
  --map LABEL=DEST  that label goes there          --dest DIR  every label without a --map
  neither, at a terminal: a folder dialog asks for each label in turn, showing where it was.
Several destinations is the normal case: map each label separately. One tidy destination for a
haphazard library is `--dest DIR --layout canonical`, which files every repository at
<DIR>/<host>/<owner>/<name> whatever folder it came from; `preserve` (default) recreates the
recorded layout under each label's destination.

Without `--apply` this prints the plan and changes nothing. An existing destination is left
alone; a repository with no recorded remote is listed for a human (`--use-candidates` lets a
URL found in its readme or project files be used); what a clone cannot restore -- uncommitted
work, unpushed commits, stashes -- is named per row. Credentials are yours: this runs
`git clone` non-interactively with the `gh`/SSH access the machine already has.
```

### scan-tree

`gitso scan-tree`, or `Special/scan_tree.py`.

```text
Read-only working-tree or staged-byte scan; Python 3.11+, Git, masked stdout.

Why:          check what is about to be committed or published before it is.
Reads:        the working tree, or the staged bytes, and the shared security policy.
May change:   nothing.
Results:      masked findings on stdout, or --json; a full private report only with --out.
Layer:        Special: this machine, once.
Status:       working

    python Special/scan_tree.py /path/to/repo --settings-home /path/to/profile --json
    python Special/scan_tree.py /path/to/repo --staged --out /private/staged.json

The settings profile owns the saved policy. --out explicitly creates a full private report; no implicit
report/log/config is written. See --help. Returns 0 checked, 1 findings, 2 incomplete/failure.
Optional --engine gitleaks/betterleaks/trufflehog may be repeated; --engine none overrides
saved selection. Engines are never installed automatically. Findings include masked location,
line, report-local id and remedy guidance; requested reports are presented as artifacts.
Full reports may use external private storage; inside Git they must be ignored/untracked.
Scoped accepted examples remain visible. review_finding.py previews/saves/revokes decisions;
changed content and coverage gaps still hold actions. No source or Git state is changed here.
--staged reads changed-file bytes from the index instead of working/untracked files. It never
stages, commits or invokes clean filters; use it to review the bytes produced by Git's staging.
```

### scan-history

`gitso scan-history`, or `Special/scan_history.py`.

```text
Read-only local reachable-history scan; Python 3.11+, Git, no fetch or rewrite.

Why:          anything ever committed stays in history, published or not.
Reads:        every commit reachable from local refs, and the shared security policy.
May change:   nothing.
Results:      masked findings on stdout, or --json; a full private report only with --out.
Layer:        Special: this machine, once.
Status:       working

    python Special/scan_history.py /path/to/repo --settings-home /path/to/profile --json

The settings profile owns the saved policy. Masked stdout is default; --out requests a full private report. --ref narrows
local reachable refs. No implicit report/log/config. Returns 0 checked, 1 findings, 2 incomplete.
Optional --engine gitleaks/betterleaks/trufflehog may be repeated; --engine none overrides
saved selection. Only already selected material is sent to an engine, without provider
verification. Masked actionable records and explicit report artifacts share the tree contract.
Full reports may use external private storage; inside Git they must be ignored/untracked.
Scoped reviews match exact finding content/location; they never clear uninspected material.
```

### review-finding

`gitso review-finding`, or `Special/review_finding.py`.

```text
Review one exact example finding without globally allowing its value.

Why:          an example value that is fine in one exact place should not hold every action forever.
Reads:        a private scan report.
May change:   with --apply and the plan id: one saved review decision in the profile.
Results:      a masked preview and result.
Layer:        Special: this machine, once.
Status:       working

    python Special/review_finding.py --help
    python Special/review_finding.py /private/scan.json finding-000001 --reason "Reviewed test example"

Preview creates no state. Rerun with --apply --approve REVIEW_PLAN_ID to save exactly that
decision under the selected user-data home. Use --revoke REVIEW_ID instead of a finding to
preview/revoke acceptance. Changed content/check/location needs review again. Prohibited
values, strong credentials and coverage gaps cannot be waived. No Git action is performed.
Default text and --json always mask values; full evidence/reasons remain in private files.
```

### clean-history

`gitso clean-history`, or `Special/clean_history.py`.

```text
DANGEROUS HISTORY MAINTENANCE: explicit cleanup into a new private mirror, never publish.

Why:          personal data published in history stays published until history is rewritten.
Reads:        a full private scan report and an explicit choices document.
May change:   only a new private mirror; never the source checkout and never a push.
Results:      a private plan, the rewritten mirror, its proof and rescan.
Layer:        Special: this machine, once.
Status:       working

    python Special/clean_history.py plan /private/history.json --choices /private/choices.json --plan-out /private/plan.json --json
    python Special/clean_history.py apply /private/plan.json --workspace /private/new-run --approve PLAN_ID

First use scan-history --out for a full private report. Planning rescans and rejects stale
refs/findings. --include-remote-refs explicitly preserves remote-only history and origin/HEAD;
without it an ordinary checkout with tracking refs is refused. No fetch or settings change.
Application requires an attended terminal and typed REWRITE, with no --yes/confirmation flag.
GUI/callable clients use the same run_cleanup function after their own human approval.

The choice document has schema_version=1 and four required lists:
replace_findings: {finding_id, new, targets: [blob,path,message], ignore_case: bool, bounded: bool}.
remove_files: finding ids selecting the WHOLE containing file/container across history.
remove_paths: literal Git paths; a trailing slash explicitly selects the directory subtree.
rewrite_identities: {finding_id, name, email}, mapping the exact selected identity pair only.
Empty lists mean no choices of that kind. Never infer purge scope from a finding or missing file.
For example (substitute an actual content-finding id from your private report):

    {"schema_version": 1,
     "replace_findings": [{"finding_id": "finding-000007", "new": "public-example",
       "targets": ["blob", "path", "message"], "ignore_case": true, "bounded": true}],
     "remove_files": [], "remove_paths": [], "rewrite_identities": []}

No raw secret is needed in the choice file. Plans/native diagnostics/full rescans stay private;
stdout and optional common reports/logs are masked/counts-only. Missing/bad settings never fall
back. Every produced artifact is presented. A verified mirror grants no publication clearance
and does not rotate credentials, fix other clones or erase external copies. Review before use.
```

### follow-rewrite

`gitso follow-rewrite`, or `Special/follow_rewrite.py`.

```text
Move this machine's clones onto a rewritten history, and update the commit ids their files quote.

Why:          after clean_history rewrites a repository and the forced push is made, every
              older clone must follow, or a push from it publishes the old history again.
Reads:        the checkouts under the given folders; the rewrite workspace's commit map.
May change:   `follow`: after one confirmation, `git reset --keep` of each safe checkout onto
              its rewritten upstream; a checkout with unpushed or uncommitted work is refused.
              `relink --write`: quoted commit ids in tracked text files, left for review.
              Nothing is committed or pushed (use commit_repo.py and push_repo.py).
Results:      plans and results on stdout.
Layer:        Special: this machine, once. Other machines: Elaborate/follow_rewrite_fleet.py.
Status:       working

    python Special/follow_rewrite.py follow [PATH ...] [--match TEXT] [--depth N] [--yes]
    python Special/follow_rewrite.py relink WORKSPACE [WORKSPACE ...] --checkout PATH [--write]
```

### secure-commit

`gitso secure-commit`, or `Special/commit_repo.py`.

```text
Preview/check and explicitly commit named files using shared security policy.

Why:          a commit should never carry a secret or a private value by accident.
Reads:        the named files and the shared security policy.
May change:   with --apply and the plan id: one commit of the named files.
Results:      a masked plan and result on stdout, or --json.
Layer:        Special: this machine, once.
Status:       working

    python Special/commit_repo.py /path/to/repo file.txt -m "Describe the change" --json
    python Special/commit_repo.py /path/to/repo file.txt -m "Describe the change" --apply --approve PLAN_ID

Python 3.11+, Git 2.36+. Preview writes no index, Git objects, report or settings. Apply uses
named working-tree contents, preserves other staged work and delegates existing traditional
hooks through a temporary per-command relay. Unreviewed hook changes hold the commit. No
persistent hook installation, automatic push or rollback. Source/metadata checks are optimistic
against other writers; unsupported Git states fail explicitly. See --help for profile options.
```

### secure-push

`gitso secure-push`, or `Special/push_repo.py`.

```text
Plan a single branch push and check its outgoing history before publishing.

Why:          publishing should check the outgoing history first, every time.
Reads:        the branch, its outgoing commits and the shared security policy.
May change:   with --apply and the plan id: one non-forced push of exactly the planned tip.
Results:      a masked plan and result on stdout, or --json.
Layer:        Special: this machine, once.
Status:       working

    python Special/push_repo.py /path/to/repo --json
    python Special/push_repo.py /path/to/repo --apply --approve PLAN_ID

Python 3.11+ and Git; --settings-home selects a profile. Preview
reads only local scope/policy, writes no files and provides no outgoing security clearance.
Apply needs the unchanged plan, fetches the selected remote and uses the same security gate as
Archive Sync. Supports one matching upstream/push destination on an existing remote branch.
No force, extra tags, other branches, hook installation or automatic commit. Masked output to
stdout, no report/log unless a later common output integration explicitly requests one.
```

### peer

`gitso peer`, or `Elaborate/peer.py`.

## App: presence and presentation

### tray

`gitso tray`, or `App/tray.py`.

```text
Run this machine's fleet peer behind a tray icon, and open its web view from the tray.

Why:          a fleet whose peers are not running knows nothing. The tray makes "is it
              running?" a glance, and stopping it deliberate rather than accidental.
Reads:        the running peer's display document every few seconds, in memory.
May change:   nothing itself. Its menu runs the same operations as the terminal: rescan,
              catch-up preview (fetch only), start at login.
Results:      a tray icon (Windows, KDE and other trays, macOS menu bar), its tooltip and
              notifications; the web view in the browser. Counts-only operational events go
              to the log the common app settings choose; console text is never written to disk.
Layer:        App: presence and presentation. Needs PySide6 (Qt).
Status:       working; the Qt window is a placeholder (App/window.py).

    python App/tray.py [--config-dir D] [--settings-home H] [--view web|window]
                       [--open-on-start] [--remote]
```

### serve-web

`gitso serve-web`, or `App/serve_web.py`.

```text
Run this machine's fleet peer with its web view and no tray; or only show published status.

Why:          some setups want the web view always on: a headless machine watched from a phone
              over the tailnet, or a desktop that prefers a browser to a tray.
Reads:        the fleet configuration. With --manifests-only: the status transport's published
              manifests and the local catalog, without running a peer.
May change:   nothing in your repositories; the peer writes its own state and manifests.
Results:      the web view at the printed address; log lines on stdout.
Layer:        App: presence and presentation. Standard library only (no Qt).
Status:       working

    python App/serve_web.py [--config-dir D] [--settings-home H] [--remote]
    python App/serve_web.py --manifests-only [--port N] [--no-browser]
```

## Setup

### setup

`gitso setup`, or `_build/setup_gitspecops.py`.

```text
Optional guided setup for gitSpecOps's command-line tools.

Run from this repository:

    python _build/setup_gitspecops.py     (or: run_setup.bat / run_setup.ps1 / run_setup.sh)

With no arguments, choose the walkthrough or an individual setup item.
Non-interactive callers must name an action; --help never performs setup.
Use settings for guided updater preferences, and settings-preview/settings-save for reviewed
noninteractive changes. The `bootstrap` action does two things:

  1. Creates a local virtual environment (.venv) with a predictable interpreter
     (and the desktop app's Qt). It prefers `uv sync` and falls back to the
     stdlib `venv` module. The project is NOT installed into .venv -- the tools
     run as scripts and there are no dependencies; an editable install would only
     add a startup-time `.pth` hook (see the note in pyproject.toml).

  2. Reports whether the runtime prerequisites (git, gh, uv) are available.

No shortcuts or launchers are written. Every command runs through `gitso.py`, e.g.
`python gitso.py commands`, or directly by its path, e.g. `python Special/update_archive.py --help`.
Auth is never touched here: users authenticate their own host CLI (`gh auth login`, ...).
```
